findings.title: _cmd_submit TOCTOU on --name uniqueness (T-07 spoofing mitigation gap)
findings.description: cli._cmd_submit checks `_name_is_taken` and then calls `store._atomic_write_json` without holding any cross-process lock. Two concurrent `python -m taskq submit --name X` invocations can each load an empty store, each pass the name check, and each persist their own record; the last write wins and silently loses the other. The check is single-process safe but multi-process unsafe.
findings.reasoning: file:line 03-development/src/taskq/cli.py:174-196 — read-modify-write of tasks.json is NOT wrapped in `STORE_LOCK` and `_atomic_write_json` is not cross-process serialised. STORE_LOCK is `threading.Lock` (store.py:29-30) and only protects within one process. Pre-fix probe: 10 concurrent submits with the same --name produced 2 accepted + 8 rejected (acceptable: 1). Post-fix probe: exactly 1 accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the load/check/write block in `with store._file_lock(home / store.TASKS_FILENAME):` (an `fcntl.flock`-based context manager in store.py).
findings.verify_evidence: test_bh_f1_concurrent_submit_unique_names RED-pre: accepts=2/10 (expected 1). GREEN-post fix: 1/10. Probe: cli.main(['submit','--name','dupname','echo job']) launched 10× via ThreadPoolExecutor of subprocess.run — 2 succeeded before the lock, 8 rejected.

findings.title: store._atomic_write_json cross-process race (T-05 corruption / data loss)
findings.description: _atomic_write_json picks a tmp file named `.{name}.{8-hex}.tmp` then in `finally:` unconditionally calls `tmp.unlink()`. Two concurrent CLI processes can both pick the same 8-hex suffix; one's `finally.unlink` removes the other's still-pending tmp file → `os.replace` raises FileNotFoundError and tasks.json may be destroyed entirely (deleted or left empty). Pre-fix probe of 50 concurrent submits via multiprocessing.Pool ended with tasks.json GONE and workers reporting FileNotFoundError on tmp → tasks.json rename.
findings.reasoning: file:line 03-development/src/taskq/store.py:51-64 — the tmp suffix is only 8 hex (32 bits) and the `finally: tmp.unlink()` runs unconditionally. STORE_LOCK is process-local. Pre-fix probe (50 concurrent submits via multiprocessing.Pool) produced 5/20 commands lost (probe1) and tasks.json destroyed entirely (probe2 with traceback FileNotFoundError '/tmp/tq_corrupt_test/.tasks.json.a0ff0ca5.tmp' -> '/tmp/tq_corrupt_test/tasks.json').
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 8-hex tmp suffix with 16-hex (uuid4 hex) AND acquire `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` on `.tasks.json.lock` for the duration of the write. Callers that do a read-modify-write MUST hold the same flock (cli._cmd_submit, store.update_task).
findings.verify_evidence: test_bh_f2_concurrent_submits_no_data_loss RED-pre: 5/20 commands lost. GREEN-post fix: 0/20. Probe multiprocessing.Pool(50): pre-fix -> FileNotFoundError on os.replace + tasks.json missing on disk; post-fix -> all 50 accepted, all 50 commands persisted.

findings.title: stdout_tail / stderr_tail persisted verbatim (T-04 information disclosure)
findings.description: _execute returns `_tail(result.stdout)` and `_tail(result.stderr)` verbatim; cache.put then persists the same dict to cache.json. A user who submits a command whose output contains an API key (`sk-*`), bearer token, or `token=...` value has that secret durably written to disk under $TASKQ_HOME/tasks.json AND $TASKQ_HOME/cache.json — recoverable by any process that reads those files. No redaction logic exists anywhere in src/taskq/.
findings.reasoning: file:line 03-development/src/taskq/executor.py:155-160 — `_tail` does no redaction; the only processing is length truncation. Pre-fix probe: submitted `python3 -c "print('sk-ZXAMPLE0123456789ABCDEF0123456789')"`, ran, and tasks.json.stdout_tail = 'sk-ZXAMPLE0123456789ABCDEF0123456789\n' verbatim; cache.json same. Post-fix probe: stdout_tail = '[REDACTED]\n'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `_redact()` helper that strips sk-*, token=*, Bearer *, password=* patterns via regex, applied before persistence. Apply to both TimeoutExpired and success-path returns.
findings.verify_evidence: test_bh_f3_subprocess_output_redacted RED-pre: re.compile(r'sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}').search(persisted) matched. GREEN-post fix: no secret-shaped substring present in tasks.json or cache.json. Probe: persisted stdout_tail='sk-ZXAMPLE0123456789ABCDEF0123456789\n' (pre) → '[REDACTED]\n' (post).

threat_model_verification.attempted_exploit: cli.main(['submit', ...]) with cmds containing `(`, `{`, `*`, `~`, `\n`, `%` (none in BLACKLIST_CHARS) — all accepted by _validate_command but executor parses with shlex.split + shell=False, so they reach the OS as literal argv and never invoke shell semantics. ; | & $ > < ` are still rejected at the validation layer as defense-in-depth.
threat_model_verification.mitigation_evidence: executor.py:140-146 uses subprocess.run(shlex.split(command), shell=False). No shlex.quote / shell=True fallback path exists. Verified by grep -rn 'shell=True' returning zero hits.

threat_model_verification.attack_vector: executor falls back to shell=True during a refactor
threat_model_verification.attempted_exploit: grep -rn 'shell=True' across src/taskq/ — zero hits; the only `shell=` reference is `shell=False` on executor.py:142. No fallback path exists.
threat_model_verification.mitigation_evidence: executor.py:140-146 — explicit shell=False; the BLACKLIST + shlex.split combination has no path that toggles shell=True.

threat_model_verification.attack_vector: subprocess hangs forever and consumes worker slots
threat_model_verification.attempted_exploit: Submitted `sleep 30` with TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT=2 → subprocess.run(..., timeout=2) raised TimeoutExpired; executor._execute caught it and returned status='timeout'/exit_code=4. Wall-clock elapsed = 4.22s (1 retry attempt per breaker.retry_limit()=2 with backoff). Single-task path returns EXIT_TIMEOUT (4) without leaking the thread. run_all path uses ThreadPoolExecutor with `with` block + fut.result() — every future completes, pool is closed at exit.
threat_model_verification.mitigation_evidence: executor.py:147-153 TimeoutExpired handler + run_all ThreadPoolExecutor context manager (line 272-275). Probe: rc=4, status='timeout', no thread leak.

threat_model_verification.attack_vector: stdout_tail / stderr_tail persisted to disk with secrets
threat_model_verification.attempted_exploit: Submitted `python3 -c "print('sk-ZXAMPLE0123456789ABCDEF0123456789')"` — secret landed verbatim in tasks.json.stdout_tail AND cache.json entry. Confirmed.
threat_model_verification.mitigation_evidence: Pre-fix: no redaction layer. Post-fix (commit e8805d0): _redact() applied to both stdout/stderr paths; sk-*, token=*, Bearer *, password=* patterns replaced with [REDACTED].

threat_model_verification.attack_vector: concurrent python -m taskq processes corrupt tasks.json on interleaved write
threat_model_verification.attempted_exploit: 50 concurrent submits via multiprocessing.Pool — pre-fix tasks.json ended deleted entirely (FileNotFoundError on tmp→tasks.json rename). 20-thread probe: 5/20 commands silently lost.
threat_model_verification.mitigation_evidence: Pre-fix: store._atomic_write_json had only an in-process threading.Lock (STORE_LOCK) and an 8-hex tmp suffix (uuid4 collision window). Post-fix: 16-hex suffix + fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) on .tasks.json.lock wrapping the entire read-modify-write. Verified by re-running the 20-thread probe — 0/20 commands lost, tasks.json valid JSON with all 20 commands.

threat_model_verification.attack_vector: schema migration overwrites v0 tasks.json without recoverable backup
threat_model_verification.attempted_exploit: No schema-migration code path exists in the current codebase; load_store returns the v1 skeleton only when tasks.json is missing entirely. A v0 file (no `version` key) is loaded as-is — no migration, no backup. The declared threat is hypothetical because there is no v1→v2 upgrade path yet.
threat_model_verification.mitigation_evidence: Threat is currently hypothetical — there is no upgrade path to exercise. The mitigation would be: when adding a v2 loader, copy tasks.json → tasks.json.v1.bak before any write. Logged as MEDIUM severity, not blocking Gate 3 (per protocol: medium/low do not block).

threat_model_verification.attack_vector: user supplies --name duplicating an existing pending/running task to silently shadow state
threat_model_verification.attempted_exploit: Single-process: _name_is_taken correctly rejects duplicate pending/running names (verified by 1 accept + 9 reject across 10 sequential submits). Multi-process: 10 concurrent subprocess submits with the same --name produced 2 accept + 8 reject pre-fix (the 2 racing processes each saw an empty store and each wrote a task record).
threat_model_verification.mitigation_evidence: Pre-fix: cli._cmd_submit used only threading.Lock (process-local). Post-fix (commit e8805d0): name-uniqueness check + write wrapped in `with store._file_lock(...)` so concurrent `python -m taskq` processes serialise. Re-probed: exactly 1 accept + 9 reject across 10 concurrent subprocess submits.
